review_findings.description: Double-counting of leeway in maxAge validation. The Validate method calls v.verifyMaxAge(claims, now, v.maxAge+v.leeway), passing leeway in the maxAge parameter, but verifyMaxAge also adds v.leeway again at line expiryPlusLeeway := iat.Add(maxAge + v.leeway). This results in the effective leeway being applied twice: maxAge + 2*leeway instead of maxAge + leeway. Fixed by passing just v.maxAge to verifyMaxAge and letting the method add leeway once internally.

The PR was applied incorrectly, causing code fragments from one file to be inserted into wrong locations in other files. For example, fragments of Validator struct fields and Validate method body appeared in errors.go and parser_option.go, and vice versa. This caused the code to not compile at all. Restored original files and re-applied changes correctly.

blue_fix.fix_explanation: 1. Reverted the corrupted files to their original state using git checkout. 2. Re-applied the PR changes correctly: (a) Added ErrTokenTooOld sentinel error to errors.go, (b) Added WithMaxAge parser option to parser_option.go, (c) Added maxAge field to Validator struct, max age check in Validate method, and verifyMaxAge method in validator.go. 3. Fixed the double-leeway bug: changed the Validate call from v.verifyMaxAge(claims, now, v.maxAge+v.leeway) to v.verifyMaxAge(claims, now, v.maxAge), since verifyMaxAge already adds v.leeway internally. Without this fix, the effective max age would be maxAge + 2*leeway instead of the intended maxAge + leeway.
